scoringModel.note: V4.2 is active. Existing 8 October selections retain V4.1 probability estimates but require a V4.2 contextual refresh before PRIME status is restored.
scoringModel.primeRule: >=55% fused win probability; market favourite; >=8pp clear of second-ranked horse; >=90% critical checks; >=5 independent positive groups; no major red flag. Handicaps additionally require retained ability and >=2 aiming groups.

scoringFrameworkV2.principle: Build a confident win decision from independent evidence groups. Value/price is assessed separately from win confidence.

establishedModel.label: Recent form & performance trend
checks: Whether recent form is improving or declining

establishedModel.label: Handicap mark, weights & claims
checks: Current OR versus last winning OR
Current OR versus best winning OR

establishedModel.label: Race targeting / placement
checks: Multiple stable runners and rider allocation

establishedModel.label: Pace, draw & likely track position
checks: Whether setup helps or hurts the horse

newcomerModel.label: Pedigree: trip / ground / surface
checks: Sire progeny strike rate at trip band
Sire progeny record on today's ground

riskDeductions.label: Strong market drift with meaningful liquidity

decisionGates.prime: 84+/100, >=90% of required checks verified, at least five independent positive evidence groups, no major red flag, and all critical checks complete.
decisionGates.fiveStar: 78-83/100 with >=85% check coverage and no unresolved critical negative.
decisionGates.pass: Do not promote as a selection if critical data is missing, contradictory evidence dominates, or the price destroys the edge.

dailyResearchProtocol: Confirm race, going, surface, distance, class, field size, draw and non-runners.
Record OR, RPR and TS where published; compare current mark with recent and winning marks.
Read last 3-5 runs, including comments and hidden trouble, not just finishing positions.
Check current trainer form over at least 14 days and recent trend.
Check trainer record at the course and in the specific race type/class/distance/surface.
Check whether the race looks deliberately suitable: alternative entries, same-race history, class/band eligibility, turnaround/layoff, race value, equipment changes and rider allocation.
Check jockey form, trainer-jockey record, horse-jockey record and whether the booking is an upgrade or meaningful choice.
Build a pace map and assess draw/track-position advantage or disadvantage.
Check market movement from early prices to current market and distinguish genuine support from thin-volume moves.
For newcomers/lightly raced horses, research sire, dam, damsire and siblings/progeny for trip, going and surface suitability before scoring.
Check the strength of recent form lines and whether horses from those races have subsequently performed well.
Record contrary evidence and risks explicitly.
Calculate check coverage; reduce confidence when evidence is missing.
Only then issue PRIME / stars and a separate VALUE label.

pilotBacktest.label: Pilot historical test
pilotBacktest.warning: 12-race exploratory sample only. Useful for direction, not statistical proof.

confidenceMethodV3.principle: Use the market as the prior probability, then move confidence only when independent pre-race evidence supports or contradicts it.
accuracyLane: Start from overround-adjusted market implied probability close to the off.
Require V2 evidence score >=84 for PRIME consideration.
Require at least five independent positive evidence groups.
Require model selection to be market rank 1 or 2 for PRIME.
No meaningful late drift; steady or shortening market is preferred.
Block PRIME if current trainer form, trainer course/race-type record, targeting, suitability or data quality is unresolved.
valueLane: Value is separate from win confidence.
Estimate model win probability from market prior plus evidence adjustments.
Only flag VALUE when model probability exceeds market implied probability by a meaningful margin after bookmaker overround.
Require score >=70 and no severe red flag.
At bigger prices, require stronger evidence or a larger probability edge; do not raise win stars simply because odds are large.
Track closing-line value: whether our advised price beats SP/BSP over time.
calibrationPlan: Backtest at least 500 races before treating star bands as calibrated.
Use walk-forward testing: train/tune on older races, test only on later unseen races.
Separate Flat, AW, jumps, 2yo/newcomer and handicap models.
Measure strike rate, ROI, A/E, Brier score, log loss and calibration by confidence band.
Record every no-bet as well as every selection to prevent hindsight filtering.
Freeze all features at a timestamp before the off to prevent data leakage.

backtest.note: ROI uses only complete SP books with 101%-140% overround. Incomplete archived betting books are excluded.

philosophy: Estimate WIN CHANCE first; assess PRICE separately.
Use the current market as a prior, not as the answer.
Only use information knowable before the race.
Targeting means observable placement evidence; never infer deliberate non-trying.
A falling handicap mark is not automatically positive. Large falls require proof that ability remains.
Missing critical data reduces confidence and can block PRIME.

probabilityEngine.description: Market prior + independent pre-race evidence, calibrated by race type.

evidenceGroups.name: Retained ability
checks: Previous RPR relative to today's OR
evidenceGroups.research: Previous RPR 5lb+ above current OR: A/E 1.08 on clean market sample.

evidenceGroups.name: Current form
checks: Running to form rather than bare finishing position

evidenceGroups.name: Trainer placement
evidenceGroups.research: Trainer course >=15%: A/E 1.05. Trainer 14-day form alone did not add value.

evidenceGroups.name: Jockey signal
evidenceGroups.research: Target-race return + jockey upgrade: A/E 1.22 in 92 clean-market runners; promising but smaller sample.

evidenceGroups.name: Handicap position
checks: Current OR vs last winning OR
evidenceGroups.research: Being 5lb+ below an old winning mark underperformed market expectation. A mark drop only counts positively when retained ability is independently proven.

evidenceGroups.name: Target-race pattern
evidenceGroups.research: Same course/time-of-year prior win: A/E 1.03; useful as supporting evidence, not standalone proof.

evidenceGroups.name: Market confirmation
evidenceGroups.research: Fusion model at >=50% probability and market top-two: 69.3% winners in 215 unseen clean-market races.

evidenceGroups.name: Pedigree / unexposed
evidenceGroups.research: Used as a prior for newcomers; confidence is capped if family evidence is incomplete.

PRIME.rule: Dynamic V4.2: favourite at >=55% generally; >=50% in maidens/novices with complete context. Context strengthens or weakens the probability rather than acting as arbitrary hard gates.
PRIME.observed: General >=55% favourite: 72.0%; maiden/novice >=50%: 71.4%; trainer/course/class context at >=55%: 78.3%.

five.rule: 45-54.9% fused win probability, with critical data complete.

one.rule: Below 20%, incomplete critical evidence, or contradictory profile.

hardBlocks: Horse is not market favourite at the final PRIME check.
Model lead over second-ranked horse is below 8 percentage points.
Unresolved non-runner, jockey, going or surface status.
Major trip/ground/surface doubt not compensated by strong evidence.
Strong recent regression with no retained-ability evidence.
Handicap PRIME lacks retained ability or fewer than two independent aiming groups.
Large mark fall is being used as the main positive without current performance proof.
For newcomers: sire/dam/sibling suitability not researched.
Material late drift or market disagreement with no plausible explanation.
Race predictability is too low: deep/uncertain race becomes NO SELECTION.

pricePolicy.rule: Do not label a horse VALUE solely because model probability exceeds market implied probability.
pricePolicy.reason: The simple value overlay lost 20.9% ROI on the clean unseen market sample, so it is not validated.
pricePolicy.currentUse: Show fair-price estimate and PRICE OK / TOO SHORT / PRICE WATCH only. Do not increase win stars because a horse is a big price.

accuracyMode.objective: Keep strong accuracy while allowing context-supported selections through.

raceTypeRules.novice: PRIME can begin at 50% when favourite and pedigree/unexposed/context checks are complete.
raceTypeRules.maiden: PRIME can begin at 50% when favourite and contextual evidence is sufficiently complete.
raceTypeRules.handicap: Normally 55%+. Emphasise retained ability, precise handicap position, class/value placement, trainer course/class record and pace.
raceTypeRules.nursery: Higher uncertainty. Normally seek ~60% or unusually strong agreement across pedigree, trainer and market evidence.
raceTypeRules.hurdle: Use stronger contextual requirements; stable form, conditions, jumping and class/grade placement matter.
raceTypeRules.chase: Normal 55% route with jumping reliability and recent completion evidence.
raceTypeRules.other: General 55% route, adjusted by class/grade/value and connection context.

latestAccuracyAudit.conclusion: Do not make aiming-group count or retained-ability a hard gate. Use them to move probability. Selectivity is driven primarily by calibrated probability, market rank and race type.

contextModel.principle: Probability first, context second. Context adjusts confidence; only historically validated factors alter thresholds.

primeRoutes.name: General
primeRoutes.rule: Favourite with model probability >=55% and core evidence complete.

primeRoutes.name: Maiden/Novice
primeRoutes.rule: Favourite with probability >=50% when unexposed/pedigree/context checks are complete.

primeRoutes.name: Trainer-Course-Class boost
primeRoutes.rule: At >=55%, strong trainer record at this course in the same class materially strengthens confidence.

primeRoutes.name: Trainer-Course-Grade boost
primeRoutes.rule: At >=55%, strong trainer record at this course in the same grade strengthens confidence.
